items.stem: A ticket router classifies five million tickets each month. Claude Haiku 5.5 clears the measured quality floor on the team's test set. The constraint: use the lowest-cost tier that clears the floor. Which choice meets the constraint?
options: Route every ticket to claude-haiku-5-5, the lowest tier that clears the floor.
Route every ticket to Claude Haiku 4.5, which costs less per million tokens than Haiku 5.5.
Route every ticket to Claude Fable 5.1, the top tier, for the highest safety margin.
Set effort to max on Claude Haiku 5.5, which moves its price to the Sonnet tier.
items.rationale: The lowest tier that clears the measured floor has the lowest price for the work. Haiku 5.5 costs 0.10 dollars per million input tokens for prompts up to 100,000 tokens.
items.trap: Fable 5.1 for every ticket looks safest, but it adds cost that the measured floor does not require.

items.stem: A code assistant runs on Claude Haiku 5.5. It misses the quality floor on about 8 percent of requests at the default effort. The team must keep the same model and raise quality with the least change. Which change meets the constraint?
options: Move all traffic to Claude Fable 5.1, which clears the floor on every request.
Raise effort to high only for the requests that miss the floor, and keep the medium default for the rest.
Set a thinking budget_tokens value of 20,000 on Haiku 5.5 to raise thinking depth.
Set effort to xhigh on every request and rebuild the eval set with extra checks.
items.rationale: Effort is set per request on the same model, so only the requests that miss the floor get more effort. Haiku 5.5 supports high effort, and its default is medium.
items.trap: A thinking budget looks like a direct depth control, but budget_tokens returns a 400 error on Haiku 5.5.

items.stem: A team runs one extraction task on Claude Haiku 5.5. Most requests clear the quality floor at the default effort. The constraint: keep cost and latency low while the quality floor holds. Which two options meet the constraint?
options: Send all traffic to Claude Opus 5.5, so every request clears the floor.
Keep Haiku 5.5 for all traffic, and set low effort for simple requests.
Set a thinking budget_tokens value on Haiku 5.5 to cut output tokens.
Escalate only the requests that miss the floor to Claude Sonnet 5.5.
items.rationale: Haiku 5.5 is the lowest-priced current model in this set and handles most requests. Low effort reduces thinking on simple requests, and escalation sends only the misses to a higher tier.
items.trap: Opus 5.5 for all traffic looks like a safe floor, but it raises cost for requests that Haiku 5.5 already clears.
